name: DiskHoard
purpose: Measures what fills the user's disks, knows which folders are regenerable junk (caches, node_modules, build output, temp files) and can clean them: to the Recycle Bin, permanently with explicit confirmation, or through a reviewable PowerShell script.
notes: Standard library only: any Python 3.9+ runs both the app and the MCP bridge, so Faustus's own interpreter is enough. The bridge starts the app itself when it is not running. The UI opens with a token in the URL; the bridge reads the same token from data/mcp-token. Deleting through the assistant goes to the Recycle Bin unless it says mode='permanent' with confirm=true, and drive roots, the user profile, Windows and anything the catalog marks 'do not touch' are always refused.
